utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Miss Hollis, would you call your next witness please?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We would call Azra Blazevic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: AZRA BLAZEVIC was called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you take that oath please, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you please state your full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Azra Blazevic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 14th November 1959.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Born in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is that the town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you live in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until 1986.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In 1986 where did you move?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you live in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 1996 (sic) to the outbreak of the war in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, was that from 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 86, I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your husband's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ermin Strikovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your husband's ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was your previous occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Veterinarian.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did you study veterinary medicine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did you practise veterinary medicine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was your practice located in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Surgery was in Kozarac, at the entrance into Kozarac, between the sawmill building and the soccer field.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If I could ask that the witness be provided with Prosecution Exhibit 196 which was the map of Kozarac, please? If that could, please, be put on the overhead projector? (To the witness): Mrs. Blazevic, in your practice as veterinarian, did people commonly refer to you as "Dr. Blazevic" or "Mrs. Blazevic"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They usually called me "Azra".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Perhaps I will call you "Dr. Blazevic". Could you please look at Prosecution Exhibit 196, this map, and if we would use the football field on the map as a point of reference, could you please show the court where your clinic was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The clinic was here. (Indicated)

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did you live in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the building of the veterinary clinic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: All right. Then looking at the football field and you pointed to a position just beneath the football field as your clinic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then if you would look below that to a road that runs from the left on the map down toward the right, was this road sometimes referred to as the new Prijedor/Banja Luka highway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you mean this road here, then, yes, that is the new road to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In which direction would Banja Luka be on this map, then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicated) Here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Which direction then would Prijedor be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The street that runs in front of the location of your house and clinic and the football field and continues up toward the mosque, was this the main street, the main business street, of the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is the street which goes through the centre of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was this street at some point at least referred to as the Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This main street going to the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, perhaps it has a different name. The high street, the main street, begins from this intersection here and then led onward to Kozara.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where is the Marsala Tita Street on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From here upward.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then that portion of the street as it runs from this intersection down past your house, what was that called?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I received all the mail and everything else came to the veterinary clinic in Kozarac. It could have been Omladinska Street.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: All right. Now if you would please look at the map again and, using the school as a reference, we see a triangular intersection there, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This road that runs through that triangular intersection there, was this sometimes referred to as the old Prijedor road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we were to go back to your house and, instead of going up the main street toward the mosque, we were to go in the opposite direction and follow this road as it crosses over the new Prijedor highway, that would lead us where? That road led where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This road here leads to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then if we are looking at this map and we look at the drawing with the "H" inside, was that the medical centre in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The mosque that is marked on this map, what mosque was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be Mutnik mosque.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then if we look at the building that is marked as a motel, was this the building that was used as a temporary medical facility during the attack on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Dr. Blazevic, did you practice only in the town of Kozarac or did you have a certain area, a geographic area, within which you practised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was covering a large area that belonged -- it was a wide, much wider area than just the town of Kozarac and that was covered by the clinic in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If the witness could be provided with Prosecution Exhibit 79, and if the Prosecution Exhibit 196 could remain with the witness but on the witness table, please? (To the witness): Could you please look at that map for a moment to familiarise yourself with it? If that could be put on the overhead projector, please? Dr. Blazevic, using this map, could you point out to the court the rough area within which you practised veterinary medicine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be here if -- if we take, if we picture that this is the centre of Kozarac, then the area in which I worked towards Prijedor came up to the road that led to Gornje Garevci and that would be the road, this would be this road here. This is the road that leads upward. If we went towards Banja Luka, the last area that I covered was the area of Jakupovici village, and that would be the road that is here. In the direction from Kozarac to Trnopolje, it would encompass all area of -- all of the Trnopolje area and then also the whole territory around Kozarac, up to Kozara and up to Mrakovica, up to those hills.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Within this geographic area that you have just discussed, did your veterinary practice take you frequently into the villages within that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you come to know many of the inhabitants of those villages through your veterinary practice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Within that geographic area that you have outlined, what was the predominant ethnic group or groups who inhabited those villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was Omarska within your geographic area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you make frequent visits to Omarska for other than business reasons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you visit Omarska at all, the village of Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How frequently would you visit that village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that often.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, how far from Kozarac was the village of Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 11 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How far was Kozarac from Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also 11 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you look again on the map, could you show us, is what is marked "4" on the map which we say was sometimes called the new Prijedor/Banja Luka road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be this road here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That is a road that has the numerical designation of "4" at some point on the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you talked about the old Prijedor road, could you show us where that would be on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be this road here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So that road led in one direction to Prijedor and in the other direction it led to where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One direction to Prijedor and the other direction went to Banja Luka -- a long time ago. I do not know if this is still so.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Dr. Blazevic, how far was Kozarac from Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Six kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I believe you indicated that that village was within your geographic area, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was the ethnic composition of the village of Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also mostly Muslim, majority of Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have indicated that you lived in Kozarac from 1986 until the attack on Kozarac. When we speak of Kozarac, there was first the town of Kozarac which was fairly small, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do some people also refer to a larger Kozarac area which would mean not just the town but also some surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the course of your living in Kozarac, would you go through this main part of town on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know many of the people who lived in the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, how well did the people in the town of Kozarac know their neighbours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fairly well.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, what was the ethnic composition of the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Majority of Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you lived in Kozarac did you know Dusko Tadic also known as Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Superficially, as one of the inhabitants of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How would you characterise your relationship with Dule Tadic? Would you say you were friends, you were acquaintances, you knew each other in passing? How would you characterise that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We knew each other by passing.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On an average during the time you lived in Kozarac, how frequently would you say that you saw Dule Tadic, for example, in a week, how frequently would you see Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not pay attention to this. I had an every day opportunity to see him, maybe even a few times a day.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Over what period of time did you have this passing acquaintance with Dule Tadic, over how many years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably all of the time, the whole time since I started working in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, where was the house of Dule Tadic in relation to your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In relation to my house, the house of Dule Tadic was in the direction when you went through the centre of Kozarac, it was on the right-hand side of the road somewhere approximately across from the pharmacy or maybe a little bit higher than that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: About how far would that be from your house, if you could estimate that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My personal view, maybe a couple of hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did Dule Tadic have a restaurant or a cafe in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was that cafe located, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This cafe was located in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to show you a video tape of a portion of Kozarac. So if Prosecution Exhibit 195 could be started at the place that I indicated, please? We are going to be stopping at various points and I will ask you to identify structures, if you can. So if we could start that video, please? Do we have that video ready to play?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could stop the video here, please? Could you tell us what this building is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Mutnik mosque.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could then, please, move the video to the return trip on the other side of the street, please? If you could stop the video there, please? Can you tell us what was located in this building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This building was the pharmacy of Kozarac, barber shop and a store.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could go forward, please? If we could stop the video here, please? What is this building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the elementary school in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could go forward, please? If we could stop the video here? Is this the triangle intersection on the map where what is called the old road, old Prijedor road, would come into the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could continue, please? If we could stop the video here, please? Pause it. What is this building, this red building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is an office that was built by one of the sons of Bozo Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know the name of this son of Bozo Dragicevic who built this office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know who this belonged to. One of the sons name was "Bosko", and he lived nearby. The other son, I think, was called "Slavko" and I think he worked in Prijedor at the post office.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: All right. If we could continue, please? This is the red building you were just referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then if we could hold it there, please? This yellowish looking building next to the red building, what building is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the house of Bozo Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where Bozo Dragicevic's house was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where would that be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is immediately next to this house in the yard that comes after this house.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So if we have the red building here and then the yellowish building is Bozo's home, and then next to that not shown on this film clip would be the home of Bozo Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could move, please, forward? If we could move to the next segment, please? If you could stop there, please? Do you recognise this building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is this building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the clinic, medical clinic, in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could continue with that, please? How was this medical centre situated in Kozarac? Was it set apart at all from the other homes around it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it is located in the part of Kozarac where private houses are located and this is the only house of this type in this area and it is located on a very small hill.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to direct your attention to 30th April 1992, the date that the Serbs -- if we could stop that, please, and that is all I want of that, please -- took over power in the town of Prijedor. How did you find out about that takeover of power?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that I heard it from the workers at the sawmill who came from Prijedor to work in the first shift.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you shortly after that become aware that Prijedor opstina had been proclaimed as a Serb opstina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you become aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People were saying that something is happening in Prijedor, that all around is the army and that at the house of -- municipal house there is a large flag with a typical Serbian sign, and in that place there always used to be the flag of former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever hear any type of formal announcement as to why intervention in Prijedor had to occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Later, during the day we heard information on the radio regarding this.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you hear on the radio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We heard information that the army has taken over the power in the municipality of Prijedor, and they were forced to do that because there was an increased danger of, as far as I could remember, Muslim extremists and something similar to this.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you actually go to Prijedor after the takeover of the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went the same day.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you see there that was different than you would have expected to see in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The city was unusually empty. One could see the military points everywhere and also this flag with four Ss on the building, municipal building.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say four Ss are you talking about the Cyrillic S?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the colour of this flag that these four Cyrillic Ss were shown on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Blue, white and red.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what flag is that? Those are the colours of what flag?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because of the characteristic sign in the middle of the flag, this flag to me represented a typical Serbian flag.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You said that the town was empty. Did you see any people at all in Prijedor on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were a couple of people there, but the city was unusually empty. Normally -- and this was in the afternoon -- normally, Prijedor is full of people.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Here you are talking about full of civilians, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers in Prijedor on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, no, I am sorry. There must be a misunderstanding. I probably did not understand the question. I said that normally in Prijedor, normally Prijedor in the afternoon hours is full of civilians, but that time when I came to Prijedor one could almost see no civilians in the streets, almost nobody was in the streets except for the army who was in various points that were all over the town.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These army personnel that you saw in Prijedor on that date, do you recall what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what kind of uniform they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you have a good memory for different types of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of these soldiers in Prijedor on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The ones that you recognised, where were they from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was the ethnic group of these soldiers that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On that date in Prijedor, did you see any combat vehicles such as tanks or amoured personnel carriers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After this date that you were in Prijedor, did you have occasion to go back to Prijedor after the Serb takeover?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On these subsequent trips to Prijedor, did you continue to notice an increased number of soldiers or police in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On any of these subsequent trips to Prijedor did you see any combat vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After the Serb takeover of Prijedor, did the Serbs also take over the leadership structure in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In the town.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So the officials in Kozarac remained the same?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As for the police in Kozarac, did all of the police remain or did some of the police leave after the Serb takeover in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, everybody remained.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After the Serb takeover in Prijedor, did the Serbs in authority there begin to give ultimatums to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were these ultimatums that were given?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were giving ultimatums to the effect that government and police in Kozarac should sign a loyalty statement to -- a loyalty statement to the government of Kozarac and take over the insignia, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were there any type of orders or ultimatums given that the people in Kozarac had to turn over weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can remember, there were such ultimatums as well.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you learn about these ultimatums which began after the Serb takeover in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During that whole period in the month of May, there were negotiations led between official government of Kozarac and Prijedor. Sometimes we could even hear comments on the radio, and most often I heard it from the people in Kozarac who would talk about it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What changes did you notice after the Serb takeover of Prijedor? What changes did you notice in your ability to travel freely in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The changes were obvious in that there was an increased control at the entry into Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say "increased control", what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean that the military checkpoints that were at the entry between the boundary line between Prijedor and Kozarac, they were stopping people -- stopping vehicles, checking the documents, the luggage and so on.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the name of this control point, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the checkpoint at Orlovci.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At what distance from Kozarac toward Prijedor was this Orlovci checkpoint located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately, four kilometres between Kozarac to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated, I believe, that the soldiers were the ones who were manning that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of these soldiers manning that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These soldiers whom you knew, where were they from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most often from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, would you like to take the 4 o'clock break now?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. We will stand in recess until 4.20.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Your Honour, in this high tech environment we operate in, there was a technical glitch earlier, so if I could have the witness shown another portion of Prosecution Exhibit 195 which the technicians did not show earlier? So if we could begin, please, with 195? (To the witness): You are switched over to the video, Dr. Blazevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could stop here, please? Do you recognise this structure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is that structure, if that could be clarified at all, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This should be the cafe of Dusan Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: All right. If we could move ahead, please? If we could stop here, please? Do you recognise this structure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this was his house.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say "his house", whose house do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dusan Tadic's.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could please shut off the film? You were talking about difficulties in movement after the Serb takeover of Prijedor. You mentioned the Orlovci checkpoint as one area where it was more difficult to pass through. Prior to the Serb takeover in Prijedor, was there a checkpoint in the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was that checkpoint located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The checkpoint was at the crossroads on the new Banja Luka road and on the road from Kozarac to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If Prosecution 196 could again be put on the overhead projector? Could you please point to the location of that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It ought to have been here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At the exact intersection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at the intersection, here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Prior to the Serb takeover of Prijedor, who manned that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: For the record, I suppose, that was where now? At the intersection of the football -- intersection of the Prijedor/Banja Luka highway and old, well, no -- that is that street we are not sure of the name of.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness pointed at the intersection of the main road that runs through Kozarac as it came past the football field and crossed what is referred to as the new Prijedor/Banja Luka highway, that intersection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Excuse me. I am sorry. Put the question again.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. (To the witness): Prior to the Serb takeover in Prijedor, who manned that checkpoint at that intersection in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the police checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The police from where manned that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the police from Prijedor and Kozarac, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So that was a mixed checkpoint with personnel from Prijedor and Kozarac manning that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After the Serb takeover in Prijedor, who manned the checkpoint at Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Policemen from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of those policemen who manned that checkpoint after the Serb takeover?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Those that you knew, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were there any other checkpoints in Kozarac itself in the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were Territorial Defence checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were those located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As a rule, at all relevant crossroads, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who would man those checkpoints in Kozarac at the main crossroads?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Members of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When were these checkpoints established?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the time exactly. It could have been the end of '91 or perhaps early '92.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The ethnic group of the people who manned those checkpoints in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The majority were Muslims but there were other ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What other ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, say, Serbs or Croats.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there any checkpoint located near the medical centre in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there a time in Kozarac where people began to guard important buildings in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not know about that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: All right. What was the date that Kozarac was attacked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 24th May.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what day of the week that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Prior to this date, prior to 24th May, had you become aware of any blockade of the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you become aware of this blockade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I was turned back from the checkpoint at Orlovci and told that I could not enter Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What date was this that this happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Thursday ---

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why were you going -- I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- it was 21st May, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you went to this checkpoint to go to Prijedor, why were you going to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was going by car and that was for the veterinary clinic to get some petrol at the petrol station in Prijedor which was the only one.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What questions were you asked at the checkpoint at Orlovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was asked where I was going to and I answered, "Prijedor". They asked me, "Why?" I told them, and showed them the order or, that is, at that time one had to have a certificate, a permission, to get a certain quantity of petrol because there was a shortage of it, and then I was asked where I was coming from and I told him "Kozarac" and then he told me that I could not go through and that I had to go back.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at this checkpoint, did you see any other vehicles which were allowed to pass through the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One vehicle did pass.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of vehicle was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A passenger vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was that civilian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A car.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was that a civilian vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise the vehicle or anyone in the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The people who were at the checkpoint at the time you were turned back, what were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Realising that you are not good with uniforms, do you recall what kind of uniforms they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think military, at least some of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At the time that you were turned back, did you know any of these people at the checkpoint, any of these people in uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The person that you knew, where was this person from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was from Kozarac or, rather, from Vidovici.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is that a village in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you happen to recall that person's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They called him Nedjo Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was that person's ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That same day that you were turned back from the checkpoint at Orlovci, did you lose any public services?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps it was before that, or slightly after that, the telephone lines were cut off.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On this same day you were turned back from Orlovci, did you notice that Serbs in Kozarac were beginning to leave Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did this Serb exodus of Kozarac continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, Thursday and Friday, as far as I know, and on Saturday.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you able to ask the Serb inhabitants why they were leaving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see them. I had only heard that they were leaving.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As these days passed, when you saw the people in Kozarac did you notice fewer Serbs among those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that the story went, whether it was on Saturday towards the evening, I think it was Saturday, that only two were still in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After you were turned back at the checkpoint at Orlovci, and the phone lines were cut and the Serbs began to leave Kozarac, what did you think was about to happen to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question. What do you mean "what happened"?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After you were turned back at the checkpoint and the phone lines were cut and Serbs began to leave Kozarac, what did you think would soon happen to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we thought that perhaps some attack on Kozarac might ensue or something like that, that the army would try and enter Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why did you think that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, simply the place was surrounded. You could not leave it. Your phones had been cut off. The Serbs were leaving and that was something that was happening already, happening before, that we used to see and because of the events that were taking place in Croatia or in east Bosnia and Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So these were familiar signs to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In preparation for this attack that you felt was soon to come, what did you and your husband do on 21st May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we, first of all, for safety reasons and because in the first place in the building of the clinic there was not a single safe room, we started thinking about where we could go; and then we decided -- I decided to go and report to the Health Centre in Kozarac or, rather, to offer them my services, the Health Centre of Kozarac, if they needed any help.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was your husband going to do in preparation for the pending attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He decided to stay with people who were at the sawmill and said that he could perhaps, since we had a car, a station wagon, that perhaps he could stay there and help if there was anybody wounded.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have mentioned the sawmill, I think, twice now in your testimony. If you could look at Prosecution 196 again and if you could point out to the court where that sawmill is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The sawmill was right at the entry into Kozarac, when one would come from Prijedor and turn towards the centre of Kozarac on the corner to the left; and between the sawmill and the football field was the veterinary clinic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you actually go to the medical centre on Thursday to begin preparations there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of preparations were done at the medical centre on the 21st?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Simply, there were several people there, there was a colleague of mine and a couple of physicians from the medical centres, and we simply tried to see in what way we could perhaps protect any of the rooms in that medical centre in case shelling would take place, so that we could gather in those rooms, and perhaps provide for some protection and get ready for the functioning in that small space.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you remain at the medical centre on 21st or did you go back home on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I went back home.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During this period between 21st May until 24th May, do you recall hearing a radio broadcast in which the ultimatum for Kozarac was restated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Some ultimatums were repeated about the return of weapons. I even think there were several of them. There was one that the deadline was extended, or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall when the deadline was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember exactly, but I think that the final deadline was sometime on Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know who was making this broadcast and repeating these ultimatums?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The then authorities of the Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When these broadcasts were made on the radio, do you recall if anything was said about what would happen if the inhabitants of Kozarac did not comply with the ultimatums?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was -- it said that if they failed to do so, then the army would have to take over Kozarac, to enter Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did Kozarac comply with the ultimatum to turn in weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what groups of people in Kozarac had weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in Kozarac policemen had weapons, both regular and Reserve force, the Territorial Defence and some people had private arms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say the police, both the regular and the Reserve, are you talking about regular and Reserve police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Regular Reserve police, active duty and Reserve strength.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that, to your knowledge, some private individuals had weapons. To your knowledge, what kind of weapons were those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, mostly hunting, as far as I know, hunting or perhaps pistols, and what else could one have?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did your husband have weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On the afternoon of 22nd May and the night of 22nd and 23rd May, did you hear or see any signs of fighting or attack from any areas close to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, what night?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This would be the afternoon of 22nd May, Friday, and the night of 22nd/early morning of 23rd May.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. On Friday afternoon, one could hear detonations from the direction of Prijedor and later on one could even see the smoke and flames rising from the area of hills in the vicinity of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were seeing these smoke and flames, what time of the day or night was this? Was this night of the 22nd, morning of 23rd?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was the night of -- evening of 22nd and in the night between 22nd and 23rd May. So, Friday to Saturday, the night between Friday and Saturday.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were you able to see these fires from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One could see it from the upper floor of the medical centre in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you use anything to assist your vision or were you looking with the naked eye?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One could see it with the naked eye, but much clearer one could see by using binoculars which Dr. Pasic had brought from his home.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So you looked through these binoculars towards the fires?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you notice anything about the way the fires were spreading, anything unusual to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the unusual thing about it was that in the beginning those fires were uneven or, rather, I mean, sometimes on the hill tops, sometimes at the foot of the hill, but then we began to see how the fire would go ablaze in series, in sort of a string, one after the other, and we assumed that somebody was setting houses on fire, one after the other.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you tell us again what the area was in which you saw these fires that appeared to be starting systematically?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are areas which are, when you go from Prijedor towards Ljubija on the hills which appear there, in that area, in the River Sana valley, next to the river.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could look at Prosecution Exhibit 79? If we could put that on the overhead and could you show the court the area in which you saw these fires?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This ought to be this area, roughly speaking. (Indicated).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That area is known to you as what area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was called Brdo or Hambarine.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. On Sunday morning in Kozarac, in the morning on Sunday, were you still free to move about as you wished?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sunday morning, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In anticipation of the attack on Kozarac, had some sort of warning signal been established for the inhabitants of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember if it was official, but I do know that on Sunday around noon when we heard the alert sounding off, when we heard it, we realised it meant some immediate, some imminent, danger of an attack.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Had there been some at least informal decision as to when that siren would be sounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could be that it was a decision to set the siren off when, I do not remember, or possibly to sound them when the police leave the checkpoint on the Banja Luka road. I remember that, because one always assumed that as long as the checkpoint of the Serb police was in Kozarac there would be no attack.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On Sunday when the siren sounded, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to the medical centre in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At the medical centre who was there when you arrived or joined you shortly after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in the medical centre that afternoon, that day, I came there, Dr. Idriz Merdzanic, Dr. Mensur Kusuran, Dr. Jusuf Pasic, my colleague, another veterinary doctor, Dr. Hase Dzonlagic, a paramedic, Mujozulic, a nurse, Sabiha Islamovic, and we were joined by some two or three girls, Lejla Hrnic, a girl by the name of Gordana, I do not know her surname, and several young men from the neighbourhood or, rather, some men from the neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These medical personnel that you have mentioned and the medical assistants that you mentioned, to your knowledge, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were all Muslims except Gordana.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was Gordana's ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did the attack on Kozarac actually begin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometime around noon on Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On Sunday, or in the days just prior to the attack on Kozarac, to your knowledge, had there been any firing from Kozarac outward, towards Serb positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, not.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, had there been any type of artillery or mortar or cannons fired from Kozarac outward towards Serb positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened when the attack began on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The attack on Kozarac started suddenly with terrible shelling which was so frequent that it seemed as though that thousands of shells are falling at the same time, and soon after that we had the first wounded people arrive.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did this shelling of Kozarac continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It lasted the whole time while I was in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That would have been until what date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would have been until Tuesday, May 26th.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there any shelling in the immediate area of the medical centre itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it seemed to us as though the whole time on purpose they were shooting exactly the medical centre.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was the medical centre itself, the building itself, ever hit by the shelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What areas of the building were damaged as a result of this shelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Due to the shelling, due to the shells that fell on the hospital itself, on the building of the medical centre or nearby, all of the windows were broken on the building, some parts of the building were damaged, for example, the front plateau of the building and I remember that a piece of the corner of the building was missing. I am talking of the medical centre building.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry. Could you please explain on the translation it says "the front plateau of the building", what do you mean by "the front plateau"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As you enter the building itself, as you enter in front of the building, there are several steps and then there is a wide plateau or a porch, and from that part you enter the building itself where the offices of some doctors are located, and on the other part there are steps that take you to the labs of the medical centre.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So then the damage you are taking about occurred on this plateau or landing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It occurred on the plateau or the building -- and the building itself.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did the damage to the building occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it happened at night, the night between Sunday and Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So this would have been the night of 24th/morning of 25th May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated earlier that the medical centre was set off somewhat from other buildings around it. Was the location of the medical centre well known to people in the larger Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At the time that the shelling of Kozarac began, what type of medical supplies did you have in the medical centre to treat wounded people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Almost none.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What supplies you did have, where did you get those supplies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The medicine and all of the material, necessary material, we used what we found in the building itself. Later on, they brought us medicine from the pharmacy in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This was the pharmacy that you earlier identified on the video tape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After the shelling of Kozarac began, were you able to see what other inhabitants of Kozarac were doing, how they were reacting to the shelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I could not see that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you remain in the medical centre itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remained until Monday.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At that time where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On Monday, we were moved into a house that all of the inhabitants of Kozarac called "motel", and it was located on the road that leads from Kozarac to Mrakovica in that area of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So this was the motel on the map, Prosecution Exhibit 196, located above the Mutnik mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why did you move to this motel on Monday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because remaining at the medical centre was practically impossible because it almost had no safe rooms and the purpose of -- there was no purpose of remaining there any more because nobody could bring us the wounded because of such frequent shelling without being wounded himself while carrying the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You mentioned that shortly after the shelling began wounded people began to arrive at the medical centre. While you were at the medical centre, how many wounded did you receive and treat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not give you the exact number, perhaps 20 or around 20.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of wounds did these people have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shelling wounds.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the age group and gender of these wounded people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Different age groups, and mostly men.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The men who were brought in who were wounded, do you recall if any of them were wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You do not recall or they were not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, they did not have uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall if any of them had weapons when they were brought into the medical centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not have weapons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of these wounded people who were brought to the medical centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, almost everyone.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of the people that you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many, if any, of these people died of their wounds before they arrived or after they were at the medical centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the building itself, one wounded died.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the age group of this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean how old was he?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe between 20 and 30 years.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew him from passing by. He was from Hrustici, I think.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On Monday when you moved to the motel, did you move the patients there as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you move them there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With a truck.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there any shelling while were you moving these patients to the motel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were any of the trucks hit by shells?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that because I went -- I was the last one to leave the medical centre with one of the drivers of the ambulance.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did any of the medical personnel remain behind at the medical centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not after me.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you moved to the motel, how long did you stay at that motel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stayed there until Tuesday morning.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many wounded did you receive after you had moved to the motel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know the exact figure, but there were many more than the first, than the first day, maybe three times more, maybe 50 or more people.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of wound did these people have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shelling wounds.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the age and gender of these wounded people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The gender, there were men and women, children as well, elderly -- there was a mixed group.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall if any of those wounded people were wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, perhaps some of them had parts of some uniforms, but I do not remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did any of these people who were brought there have any weapons with them when they came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody had arms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Almost everyone.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of these wounded people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did any of these people die either being brought to the motel or while they were at the motel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had a lot of dead people there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the age group of the people who died?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was quite varied; a child, a 12 year old child died and an elderly woman that was perhaps 70 or 80 years old.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The nature of the wounds of the people who were brought to you, what types of wounds did they have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shelling wounds.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what physical injuries to their bodies did they have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly very serious wounds, either amputations of limbs, parts of the bodies or completely shattered parts of the body.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of medical supplies or equipment did you have to deal with these persons who had amputations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at the motel what other group was also at the motel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were members of the police department in Kozarac; members of the police departments in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, who was the commander of the police there at the motel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somebody who was called Osme.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time you were at the motel did you ever overhear any negotiations taking place between these police and Serb authorities outside the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were you able to overhear these negotiations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The negotiations were led through some kind of a radio station, and since it was in the building itself in the motel, at one point I was present in one of the rooms ----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- where the negotiations were led.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry. How long did these negotiations continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that. Probably all night.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now the one time that you were present while negotiations were being carried on, who was the spokesman for the people of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Osme.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And who was he talking to or addressing over the radio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that he talked with Simo Drljaca and with Zeljaja.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know because in one part of the conversation we heard the comment for us to be more quiet because at that moment he was talking to Simo Drljaca, and the second time was because Osme yelled and requested to talk to Zeljaja.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What conditions, if any, were imposed on the inhabitants of Kozarac in order for the shelling of the town to stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The conditions were to surrender members of police with their arms, and if they go first then civilians would be allowed to leave Kozarac in a column.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When was this initial agreement or condition made, what time of the night or day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was at night, after midnight, between Monday and Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How much time were you given to gather people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard that they were given from, they were given 30 minutes to prepare the police and to form a column that was supposed to leave Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then at the end of this 30 minutes what was to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was said that they would wait for further directions, and after a certain time the connection was established again and we heard a conversation again and they asked: "Has this been done?" Osme replied: "Yes".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that we heard again frequent shelling nearby and we heard that the shells were falling on the road that led through Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could look again at Prosecution Exhibit 196, which is the map, if that could be placed on the overhead, please. Now looking at the motel area -- if that could please be reduced, thank you -- looking at the motel area where you were, would you please point out to the court where the people were to gather on the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be on this road here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On that section of the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicated). Yes, at that part of the road.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then when the shelling began again, would you please show the court where, in what area the shells were landing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I heard, in this part of the road.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you actually hear this shelling when it began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did it sound as though it was very close?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was in the immediate vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then I believe you indicated people came back into the motel and said the shelling was occurring on that road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Later on that morning, was a final agreement reached which would allow the wounded and civilians to leave Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was this agreement? What was supposed to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As it looked, I am not sure what the definite agreement was, but in early morning hours on Tuesday a group of policemen got ready and they decided to surrender. The whole time the negotiations were led to allow us to take out the wounded people that at that time were in the motel in Kozarac, and to allow us to transfer them into the hospital in Prijedor. After them a column of civilians was supposed to follow.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So early in the morning of 26th May did such a column begin to form?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did it begin to form? If you could again refer to the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It started forming exactly on this road here, up here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that could be shown on the screen, please. Could you show us again, please, where that column began to form?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this part of the road.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In what direction then did that column move?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It moved through the centre of Kozarac towards the Banja Luka road.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And who was leading that column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After the police who was in the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, our wounded people.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were the wounded to be transported?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a truck and one ambulance vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: About what time of the morning, if you know, did this column form up and begin to move down from the motel area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly. It was early in the morning, perhaps 7 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you go with the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that the wounded were being transported in a truck and an ambulance. Who were the drivers of these vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were transferred in a truck and the ambulance vehicle. The drivers, the driver of the truck was Fehim Sinanegic and the ambulance vehicle was driven by my husband and they were the volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When your husband left with that column driving the vehicle, when was the next time you saw your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In December '92.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After this column moved out, who remained behind with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So no other medical personnel remained behind with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. I did not understand. Medical personnel remained, the medical personnel that came from the medical centre in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So those individuals you have previously mentioned remained with you at the motel when the column left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the column left, when we sent out the wounded, then we decided to go back to the medical centre building in Kozarac, and since shelling had almost ceased at that point to see what we are to do from there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On the same date, 26th May, did you go to Trnopolje to attempt to negotiate with the Serb authorities there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who went with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dr. Idriz Merdzanic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is he commonly referred to as Dr. Idriz?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why did you want to confer with the Serb authorities in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We wanted actually to try to establish contact with Serb authorities and to let them know that we would like to remain in medical centre in Kozarac until civilians leave Kozarac, so that we could help these people if they should need help.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you able to speak with the Serb authorities in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So that then did you return back to the medical centre this same day, Tuesday 26th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the medical centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stayed until the afternoon when the army entered Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened at the medical centre that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That afternoon the soldiers entered into the medical centre in Kozarac, and then we had to leave the building.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These soldiers who entered into the medical centre, how many soldiers came into the area where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At first two soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you hear any of these soldiers talking or saying anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise the dialect or accent as a local dialect or as a different dialect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they spoke in Ekevica dialect.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That dialect is spoken where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened after these two soldiers came into the area where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They asked us where are our weapons, our wounded. They searched us.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were these soldiers wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After they asked you these questions, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They ordered us to collect all medicines that were at the entrance into the building. They were spread all over the entrance and those were the medicines that were brought from the pharmacy in Kozarac. They ordered us to load those medicines into the truck which we have done, and after that we left the building, the medical centre in Kozarac. They took us towards the centre of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These two soldiers who came into the area where you were, you said they spoke with Serbian dialects. Did you know either of these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you subsequently learn the name of one of those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When was it that you learned the name of one of those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of those two soldiers came again to Trnopolje, maybe even two times, and at that time spoke to us and introduced himself.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what was his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ljubomir or Ljubo Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did Stojanovic tell you where he came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he said he was from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time that you were at the medical centre, was Gordana still there with you? Was she one of the individuals with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the soldiers asking Gordana to leave the building with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, immediately after they entered one of the soldiers asked her, called her and asked her to come out, and she came back after about, perhaps, half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was her condition when she returned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was distressed, almost hysterical.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did she tell you what had happened while she was gone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We asked what had happened and where had they taken her, and all she said was that she had to show them her flat.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That she had to show the soldiers her flat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did they tell her why they wanted to see her flat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, so that they would not touch it. That is how she put it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this may be a good point to stop.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stop. I want to talk with the lawyers about the delayed transmission equipment just a moment. So, perhaps the Doctor could leave. You are excused for the day. You should return tomorrow at 10 a.m. please. (The witness withdrew).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The delayed transmission equipment is operative, I understand, and instructions are being prepared for we lay persons who have difficulty sometimes with technical equipment, but the instructions are being prepared so that we will know how to work together with them. The instructions will be completed tonight, probably about 6.30 p.m. So if Counsel is either in the building or if you want to send someone over and see Miss Featherstone, she will be able to give us those instructions. If not, you may wait until tomorrow morning and pick them up from her. I think it would be helpful tomorrow morning for us to talk a few minutes about how we might handle matters that might arise because of the need for the delay transmission commitment. So, unless there are other matters that need to be brought to the attention of the Trial Chamber at this time, we will adjourn until tomorrow at 10 a.m. (The court adjourned until the following day).

procedural_notes.text: (closed session-released by Trial Chamber II on 30 August 1996)
(The court adjourned for a short time)
